title: Setters that guard their fields

blocks.text: The course's `Person` keeps its fields private and lets callers change them only through setters that **validate** their input, so the object can never hold a bad value.

items: `setName(String name)` stores the name **without surrounding spaces**. A `null` name, or one that is empty after trimming, is refused with `IllegalArgumentException("Name cannot be null or empty")`.
`setAge(int age)` accepts `0` to `150`, both included. Anything else is refused with `IllegalArgumentException("Age must be between 0 and 150")`.

blocks.text: A refused call leaves the stored value as it was.

setName("  Jane Doe  ");  getName()   -> "Jane Doe"
setAge(30);               getAge()    -> 30
setName(null)                         -> IllegalArgumentException
setAge(151)                           -> IllegalArgumentException

cases.says: A valid name and age are stored and read back through the getters.
Spaces around a name are removed before it is stored.
A null name is refused with an IllegalArgumentException, not a NullPointerException.
A name of only spaces is refused, and the name already stored stays.
Ages 0 and 150 are accepted, while -1 and 151 are refused.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A setter decides a policy for null, and rejecting it means an IllegalArgumentException rather than a NullPointerException.
A setter validates its input before storing it, so the object never holds an invalid value.
